arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API using a bot token to send messages, list channels and conversations, read message history, manage threads, members, and reactions, search messages, and call any other Slack API method. Use when the user wants to automate Slack tasks such as posting messages, fetching channel history, listing workspace users or channels, replying in threads, or invoking Slack Web API endpoints.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

This skill wraps the entire Slack Web API through one deterministic, dependency-free script: `scripts/slack_api.cjs`. Point it at any API method (e.g. `chat.postMessage`, `conversations.list`, `conversations.history`, `users.list`) with a JSON body, and it returns the JSON response.

## Authentication

The script needs a Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) with the scopes required by the methods you call:

- Set the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable, or
- Pass `--token xoxb-...` per invocation.

See `references/api.md` for the scope required by each common method.

## Quick Start

Run from the skill directory (adjust the path if running from elsewhere):

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"#general","text":"Hello from Gemini CLI"}'
```

Common operations:

| Operation | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Send a message | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"#general","text":"Deploy finished :white_check_mark:"}'` |
| List channels | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel","limit":200}' --paginate` |
| Read channel history | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C1234567890","limit":50}'` |
| Read thread replies | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.replies '{"channel":"C1234567890","ts":"1712345678.000000"}'` |
| List users | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.list '{"limit":100}' --paginate` |
| Search messages | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs search.messages '{"query":"deploy failed","count":20}'` |
| Join a channel | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.join '{"channel":"C1234567890"}'` |
| Add a reaction | `node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add '{"channel":"C1234567890","name":"thumbsup","timestamp":"1712345678.000000"}'` |

## Workflow

1. Decide which Web API method performs the task (see `references/api.md` for the method cheatsheet and error codes).
2. Run the script with the method and a JSON body.
3. Interpret the response:
   - Success: the script prints the JSON response (contains `"ok": true`) to stdout and exits 0.
   - Failure: the script prints a single `Failure: <message>` line to stderr and exits 1.

## Guidance

- **Channel IDs (`C...`) are more reliable than channel names.** Resolve a name to an ID with `conversations.list` before posting to it.
- **Message formatting**: use Slack mrkdwn (e.g. `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|link>`) in `text`, or pass `blocks` for rich layouts. Use `\n` for line breaks inside a single-quoted JSON body.
- **Threads**: pass `"thread_ts"` in `chat.postMessage` to reply inside a thread; read the thread with `conversations.replies`.
- **Pagination**: list endpoints return up to `limit` (max 200 for most) results plus `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Use `--paginate` to fetch and merge every page automatically.
- **Rate limits**: Slack returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header. The script reports this; wait the indicated delay before retrying.
- **Escaping**: always pass the JSON body as a single-quoted shell string to avoid quoting issues.
- **Large responses are truncated** to 20,000 characters to keep context small; rerun with `--no-truncate` when the full payload is needed.
- **Token scopes**: a `missing_scope` error means the app needs an additional scope and must be reinstalled to the workspace.

## Reference

- `references/api.md` — method cheatsheet with required scopes, rate-limit tiers, common error codes and fixes, pagination details, and message-formatting tips.

# Slack Web API Reference

Table of contents:
- [Authentication and scopes](#authentication-and-scopes)
- [Method cheatsheet](#method-cheatsheet)
- [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Common errors and fixes](#common-errors-and-fixes)
- [Message formatting](#message-formatting)

## Authentication and scopes

Use a bot token (`xoxb-...`) from a Slack app installed in the target workspace. The token must include the scope required by each method, or Slack returns `missing_scope` (the response includes the `needed` scope name). Scopes are granted in the app's "OAuth & Permissions" page; after changing scopes the app must be reinstalled to the workspace.

Pass the token with `--token` or set `SLACK_TOKEN` in the environment; the skill script reads it automatically.

## Method cheatsheet

| Method | Purpose | Required scopes | Key parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage` | Post a message | `chat:write` | `channel`, `text` (or `blocks`), optional `thread_ts` |
| `chat.update` | Edit a message | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts`, `text` |
| `chat.delete` | Delete a message | `chat:write` | `channel`, `ts` |
| `chat.getPermalink` | Get a message link | none | `channel`, `message_ts` |
| `conversations.list` | List channels/DMs | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` | `types`, `limit`, `cursor` |
| `conversations.info` | Channel metadata | `channels:read` | `channel` |
| `conversations.history` | Message history | `channels:history` | `channel`, `limit` (max 200), `cursor` |
| `conversations.replies` | Thread replies | `channels:history` | `channel`, `ts` |
| `conversations.join` | Join a channel | `channels:join` | `channel` |
| `conversations.leave` | Leave a channel | `channels:manage` | `channel` |
| `conversations.create` | Create a channel | `channels:manage` | `name`, `is_private` |
| `conversations.invite` | Invite members | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `users` (comma-separated IDs) |
| `conversations.kick` | Remove a member | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `user` |
| `conversations.rename` | Rename a channel | `channels:manage` | `channel`, `name` |
| `conversations.archive` / `unarchive` | Archive/unarchive | `channels:manage` | `channel` |
| `users.list` | List workspace users | `users:read` | `limit`, `cursor` |
| `users.info` | User details | `users:read` | `user` |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | Find user by email | `users:read.email` | `email` |
| `reactions.add` | Add a reaction | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` |
| `reactions.remove` | Remove a reaction | `reactions:write` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` |
| `search.messages` | Search messages | `search:read` | `query`, `count`, `cursor` |
| `files.upload` | Upload a file | `files:write` | `channels`, `content` (or `file`) |
| `api.test` | Validate token/connectivity | none | - |

Scope notes:

- `chat:write` lets a bot post as itself. `chat:write.public` is required to post to public channels the bot has not joined; `chat:write.customize` adds custom bot names/icons.
- History scopes are per conversation type: `channels:history` (public), `groups:history` (private), `im:history` (DMs), `mpim:history` (group DMs).

## Rate limits

Slack applies tiered rate limits per app. Common tiers:

| Tier | Rate | Typical methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 | 1+ request/second | `chat.postMessage`, `reactions.add`, `conversations.info` |
| Tier 2 | 20+ per minute | `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`, `search.messages`, `users.info` |
| Tier 3 | 50+ per minute | `conversations.list`, `users.list`, `conversations.members` |
| Tier 4 | 100+ per minute | `auth.test`, `api.test` |

On HTTP 429 the script reports the `Retry-After` header value; wait that long before retrying. Bursts can also trigger `ratelimited` errors — back off exponentially (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s).

## Pagination

List-style endpoints return a `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more results exist. Pass it back as the `cursor` parameter until it comes back empty. `limit` caps results per page (max 200 for most methods).

The skill script's `--paginate` flag automates this for endpoints that return a top-level array (e.g. `channels`, `members`, `users`, `files`) and merges all pages into one response. `search.messages` paginates differently (its results live under `messages.matches`); pass `cursor`/`page` manually for searches.

## Common errors and fixes

| Error | Meaning / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token missing, expired, or revoked. Check the token and app installation. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a required scope; the response includes `needed`. Add the scope and reinstall the app. |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot is not a member. Join with `conversations.join` (public channels) or use a token with `chat:write.public`. |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad channel ID, or the bot cannot see the channel. Verify with `conversations.info`. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive with `conversations.unarchive`. |
| `invalid_arguments` | A parameter has the wrong type or is missing. Check the JSON body. |
| `invalid_ts_latest` / `invalid_ts_oldest` | Timestamps must be Slack message timestamps like `1712345678.123456`. |
| `name_taken` | Channel name already exists; channel names are unique per workspace. |
| `user_not_found` | User ID is wrong or the user is not in the workspace. |
| `already_in_channel` | Member is already in the channel (usually harmless). |
| `rate_limited` | Slow down; see rate limits above. |
| `internal_error` | Slack-side issue; retry with backoff. |

## Message formatting

- mrkdwn (default in `text`): `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, ```preformatted```, `>quote`, bullets (lines starting with `• `).
- Links with labels: `<https://example.com|Click here>`; bare URLs are auto-linked.
- Mentions/links: `<@U1234567890>` mentions a user, `<#C1234567890>` links a channel, `<!here>` / `<!channel>` notify the channel.
- Emoji: `:white_check_mark:`, `:rocket:`, etc.
- Rich layouts: pass a `blocks` array (section, divider, actions, context, image) instead of `text`. Keep `text` as a fallback for notifications and accessibility.
- Line breaks in JSON bodies: use `\n` inside the JSON string (single-quoted in the shell).
- Threads: include `"thread_ts"` in `chat.postMessage` to reply in a thread; read the thread with `conversations.replies`.
